title: Assemble the Batch From a Messy Day
subtitle: One approved invoice, four consciously held
scenario: It is 2:00 PM. The cutoff is 3:00 PM. Five invoices arrived, but only INV-59001 auto-approved - the other four are working through exceptions. Build the batch record so it shows exactly one payable invoice and honestly counts the four that are held out.
input: Approved for payment: INV-59001 (V-1042, 1200.00), auto-approved. Held in exceptions: INV-59002 (price), INV-58962 (duplicate), INV-59004 (unknown vendor), INV-59005 (missing receipt) - 4 held. Batch date: day-1. Payment cutoff: 3:00 PM. The batch gathers only approved invoices, counts and totals them, and records how many are held.
instructions: Record the batch date and the payment cutoff.
Count only the approved invoices and total their amounts (INV-59001 only).
Record heldCount for the four invoices still in exceptions - excluded, not lost.
Return one valid JSON object. Use numbers for the counts and total.
copilotPrompt: Produce a payment-batch JSON record from a messy day: batchDate, cutoff, invoiceCount, batchTotal, and heldCount. Only INV-59001 is approved; four invoices are held in exceptions.
successMessage: Payment batch assembled. One approved invoice at $1,200.00, four held - ready for run approval.
editorHelper: Gather only the approved invoice; count the four that are held.

intro.heading: Before the run: gather only what is clean

sections.title: The batch is honest about what is held
sections.body: Four of today's five invoices are still in exceptions. The batch includes just INV-59001, but heldCount records that four were consciously excluded - visibility, not silence, is what makes the run trustworthy.

sections.title: Count and total from the included invoices only
sections.body: invoiceCount and batchTotal recompute from what is actually in the batch - one invoice at 1200.00 gives a count of 1 and a total of 1200. The held invoices contribute nothing to these figures.

sections.title: The cutoff still governs the day
sections.body: The batch is assembled against the 3:00 PM cutoff. If a held invoice is resolved after cutoff, it waits for tomorrow's batch - the same deadline applies whether the day is clean or messy.

fieldGuide.meaning: The day the batch is for.
The payment cutoff time the batch is assembled against.
fieldGuide.hint: The 3:00 PM cutoff stated in the scenario.

fieldGuide.meaning: How many approved invoices are in the batch.
The sum of the batch's invoice totals.
fieldGuide.hint: One invoice at 1200.00 gives a total of 1200.

fieldGuide.meaning: How many invoices are held in exceptions and excluded.
fieldGuide.hint: Four invoices are still in exceptions today, so 4.

takeaway.heading: Payment batch assembled
points: You gathered the one approved invoice into a batch the AP Manager can approve in a single action.
heldCount records the four invoices still in exceptions - excluded on purpose, not lost.
The count (1) and total (1200) recompute from the included invoice, not the whole inbox.
The batch is built against the real 3:00 PM cutoff, saved as payment-batch.json.
The workflow can now present a messy day as one honest, totaled batch with its holds visible.
